title: LG Electronics Joins NVIDIA Partner Network for AI Data Center Cooling (KRX: 066570)
content:
Korea Supply Chain Brief · September 27, 2026

LG Electronics (KRX: 066570) says it has been named an official NVIDIA partner for AI data center cooling. Here is what LG actually supplies, where those parts sit inside an AI data center, and how solid the claim is.

CompanyWhat it suppliesEvidence
LG Electronics
KOSPI: 066570		Chillers and coolant distribution units (CDUs) for AI data centersAnnounced (company statement, reported by Korea Economic TV, Sep 27, 2026)

What happened

  • LG Electronics said it joined the NVIDIA Partner Network (NPN) in the "Power and Cooling" category, which links NVIDIA with companies that build AI data centers and "AI factories."
  • LG said its 600 kW and 1 MW CDUs met NVIDIA's specification approval, and described itself as the first Korean company to do so.
  • LG said its 2.5 MW CDU received NVIDIA's "DSX Ready CDU" certification.
  • The company pointed to North America, which it said accounts for more than 60% of new data center capacity demand, as its main target, along with hyperscale cloud and colocation operators.

Where these parts sit in an AI data center

AI servers built on NVIDIA's latest chips run too hot for air cooling alone, so racks are increasingly cooled with liquid. Two pieces of equipment in that loop are what LG is talking about:

PartJobAnalogy
ChillerMakes cold water for the whole facilityThe building's refrigerator
CDU (coolant distribution unit)Takes that facility water and runs a separate, tightly controlled coolant loop to the server racks, managing flow, pressure and temperatureThe pump-and-thermostat box between the refrigerator and each rack

The kW and MW figures describe how much heat one CDU can carry away. A 1 MW unit can serve roughly the heat load of several high-density AI racks; a 2.5 MW unit is sized for larger halls.

Why it matters for LG Electronics

Most investors know LG Electronics for TVs and home appliances. The cooling business sits in its ES (Eco Solution) division, the unit that makes air-conditioning and HVAC systems. Being listed as an NVIDIA cooling partner puts LG's HVAC know-how in front of data center builders who design around NVIDIA hardware. The announcement does not include order sizes, customers or revenue figures, so the financial impact cannot be measured from this news alone.

How solid is this?

  • Confirmed by the company: the partner listing, the CDU specification approvals, and the "DSX Ready" certification.
  • Company outlook, not results: plans to target North American hyperscalers and colocation operators.
  • Not disclosed: customers, contract values, delivery volumes.

Quick FAQ

Is LG Electronics an NVIDIA supplier?
According to LG's announcement, it is an official NVIDIA partner for data center power and cooling. That is a partner-network listing and product certification, not a disclosed supply contract.

What is a CDU?
A coolant distribution unit. It moves liquid coolant between a data center's chilled-water system and its server racks.
